question: ________ in the IUPAC nomenclature system is considered to be a derivative of hydrocarbons in which a hydrogen atom is replaced by -OR -OAr groups, where R and Ar represent alkyl and aryl groups, respectively.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ethers**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ethers **in the IUPAC nomenclature system are considered to be a derivative of hydrocarbons in which a hydrogen atom is replaced by -OR -OAr groups, where R and Ar represent alkyl and aryl groups, respectively.
 
• Common names of **ethers are derived from the names of alkyl/aryl groups **written as separate words in alphabetical order and adding the word ‘ether’ at the end.
 
• For example, **CH₃OC₂H₅ is ethylmethyl ether.**
 
• If both the alkyl groups are the same, the prefix ‘di’ is added before the alkyl group. For example, **C₂H₅OC₂H₅ is diethyl ether.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Phenol **is an aromatic organic compound characterized by a hydroxyl (―OH) group attached to a carbon atom that is part of an aromatic ring.
 
• **Alcohol **is an organic compound in which at least one hydroxyl group(-OH) is attached to the Carbon atom of the alkyl group.
 
• **Aldehyde **is an organic compound containing a functional group with the **structure − CHO, **consisting of a carbon double-bonded to oxygen with the carbon atom also bonded to hydrogen.
